strengths: Novel physics-informed approach: Encoding time-varying physical processes (shading, convection, vegetation) directly as hard structural constraints in graph topology is creative and demonstrates 23× better gains than soft PINN-style constraints (ΔR²=0.0696 vs 0.0030)

Rigorous experimental validation: Comprehensive baselines across 4 paradigms, extensive ablations isolating each component, proper generalization testing (spatially distinct test blocks, city-scale validation r=0.842, cross-domain UWF3D experiments)
Dataset contribution: UMC4/12 with 11.9M data points across 396 urban blocks, validated against field measurements (r>0.73) and city-scale reference data; genuine community resource
Computational efficiency gains: 73.8% FLOPs reduction and 21% faster training vs LRGCN baseline while maintaining superior accuracy (R²=0.8542 vs 0.8422)
Thorough documentation: Extensive appendices with parameter justifications, sensitivity analyses, implementation details; honest discussion of limitations and future work (proposed hybrid topology)
weaknesses: Training data limitation: All data from single extreme heat day with one meteorological scenario; no seasonal/temporal diversity in training set. This critically constrains generalization claims for microclimate modeling, which should vary with weather patterns. Multi-day/multi-season training would significantly strengthen the work.

Physics parameter justification: Hand-tuned parameters (shadow extent 15/5 grids, vegetation radius 5 grids, λ_wind=0.3) sourced from literature without domain-specific optimization for Singapore's microclimate. No systematic sensitivity analysis on these physics parameters (only k and data volume tested). Transferability to other cities/climates unclear.

Modest performance improvements: 1.2% R² gain over LRGCN (0.8542 vs 0.8422); RMSE≈1.05 UTCI with no discussion of practical significance for thermal comfort applications. Improvements are reliable but incremental for applications requiring high confidence.

Limited architectural novelty: RGCN from Schlichtkrull et al. (2017), LSTM standard; primary contribution is graph construction strategy rather than neural architecture design. Framing as architectural contribution slightly overstates novelty scope.

Generalization concerns: Single-location micro-scale validation (one campus), single-city dataset (Singapore only), all training from synthetic ENVI-met data. UWF3D cross-validation uses different synthetic CFD regime. No validation across different climates, latitudes, or urban morphologies.

Temporal evaluation scope: Only 12-hour prediction horizon; no long-term experiments (24h, weekly). Figure 5b shows concerning error increase during afternoon hours. Limited error accumulation analysis. Multi-task learning fails dramatically (R²=0.8629 single-task vs 0.7460 multi-task), suggesting heterogeneous message passing isn't effectively decoupling physics.

Baseline fairness concerns: Different loss formulations across models (GAE with KL divergence, CGAN with adversarial loss); hyperparameters differ between main comparison (hidden=128) and ablations (hidden=384); no statistical significance tests between methods, only standard deviations reported.

Missing practical comparisons: No wall-clock inference time vs ENVI-met; no demonstration of real-time deployment; unclear when this learned approach is preferable to running physics-based simulations that are already computationally tractable.
